name: compression-lab-category-portfolio-v1
result_policy: A category is won only after a frozen unseen-data pass against its strongest reproduced ratio baseline, its practical speed baseline, and every integrity, memory, portability, and accounting gate. Independent reproduction is required before a state-of-the-art claim.
scorecard_required_fields: complete compressed bytes and byte-weighted ratio
compression and decompression MB/s with timing basis
peak memory or an explicit unmeasured marker
per-standard win, loss, mixed, or untested outcome

categories.label: JSON and machine-generated logs
categories.current_result: Ratio passed decisively against zstd-9 and PBC-only and passed Brotli-11 in aggregate; overall gate failed Brotli family coverage and Linux decompression speed.
categories.next_gate: Profile and improve Linux decode using development data only, then freeze an independently sourced JSON/log corpus; never tune or rerun on Hadoop, OpenSSH, or OpenStack.

categories.label: Plain text and source code
categories.current_result: No category win. Existing general candidate remains behind strongest ratio baselines on the expanded public study.
categories.next_gate: Research a new text representation or probability model and freeze separate source-code and natural-language development families before integration.

categories.label: Tabular CSV and delimited records
categories.current_result: On the frozen first public-validation score over four previously unseen CC-BY-4.0 UCI families, TBS1 beat the strongest exact per-family baseline by 7.35% to 16.50% on 3/4 families, but OCRB pixel tables were 32.15% larger and made aggregate output 3.48% larger than 7-Zip-9. Average speed, cold memory, exactness, determinism, fallback safety, portability, and complete accounting passed; one of five decompression repetitions missed the 250 MB/s floor. The overall gate did not pass.
categories.next_gate: Retain the failed first score and never tune or rerun on MetroPT, electricity, OULAD, or OCRB. Treat image-like pixel matrices as a separate category, develop any successor selector or representation only on fresh development families, and require a new untouched validation corpus.

categories.label: Numeric arrays and time-series data
categories.specialist: DMS2/DSS1 for byte-exact dense numeric matrices; time-series specialist remains open
categories.current_result: On 4,895,341 fresh licensed development bytes, DMS2 was 5.28% smaller than bzip2-9 at 54.85 MB/s compression and 268.18 MB/s decompression. Local operational gates and Linux/macOS/Windows full-suite and native-wheel reproduction passed. The exact Gisette/Madelon first-score package is locked but those validation bytes remain unopened.
categories.next_gate: Run the locked Gisette/Madelon score exactly once and retain it regardless of outcome. Treat time-series, floating-point arrays, sparse arrays, and missing-value scientific data as separate future wedges with their own licensed development and unseen-validation families.

categories.label: General binary files and mixed archives
categories.current_result: No win against zstd-9; the current general encoder is not Pareto-optimal.
categories.next_gate: Retain safe direct/store fallback while category specialists mature; do not spend ratio research on a universal transform without a new measured hypothesis.

categories.label: Incompressible and already-compressed data
categories.current_result: Safety behavior is tested, but there is no category speed, memory, or large-file validation scorecard yet.
categories.next_gate: Freeze expansion, selector-cost, throughput, and large-file memory gates on licensed compressed-media and cryptographic-random families.
